topic: Glaw Lake becomes India's 101st Ramsar Site

subtopics.title: Glaw Lake and India's Ramsar Network
subtopics.summary: Glaw Lake, a pristine freshwater lake in the Eastern Himalayas region of Arunachal Pradesh, became India's 101st Ramsar Site. It lies in the protected area of Kamlang Tiger Reserve and Wildlife Sanctuary.
facts: Glaw Lake became India's 101st Ramsar Site

Type: pristine freshwater lake

subtopics.title: Wetlands: Meaning and Types
subtopics.summary: A wetland is an area of land covered by water, whether salt, fresh or in between, either seasonally or permanently. Wetlands take many forms, from lakes and rivers to mangroves and coral reefs. The booklet classifies them into three segments: inland, coastal and human-made wetlands.
facts: Wetland: land covered by water that is salt, fresh or in between
The water cover may be seasonal or permanent
Includes lakes, rivers, underground aquifers and swamps
Includes wet grasslands, peatlands, deltas and tidal flats
Includes mangroves, coral reefs and other coastal areas
Other forms: marshes, bogs, mudflats, ponds, billabongs, lagoons, floodplains
Segment 1: inland wetlands
Segment 2: coastal wetlands
Segment 3: human-made wetlands

subtopics.title: Ramsar Convention and Montreux Record
subtopics.summary: The Ramsar Convention, formally the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance, is an intergovernmental treaty adopted in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran, and in force from 1975. It has 172 member states, and India became a signatory on 1 February 1982. The Montreux Record, launched in 1990, lists Ramsar sites where ecological character has changed or is likely to change.
facts: Official name: Convention on Wetlands of International Importance
Adopted in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran; came into force in 1975
Members: 172 States
India became a signatory on 1 February 1982
World Wetlands Day: 2 February
2026 theme: Wetlands and Traditional Knowledge: Celebrating Cultural Heritage
Conference of Parties (COP) meets every 3 years
Montreux Record: launched 1990; lists sites with ecological change from technological developments, pollution or human interference
Indian sites in Montreux Record: Keoladeo National Park (Rajasthan) and Loktak Lake (Manipur)
Largest Ramsar site in the world: Pantanal, South America

subtopics.title: Government Initiatives to Preserve Wetlands
subtopics.summary: The Amrit Dharohar Capacity Building Scheme is a joint effort of the Ministry of Tourism and MoEFCC to make optimal use of wetlands. The Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017 provide a regulatory framework under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. The Wetland City Accreditation Program, approved at COP 12 in 2015, recognises cities that conserve urban wetlands.
facts: Amrit Dharohar: joint effort of the Ministry of Tourism and MoEFCC
Amrit Dharohar aims: optimal wetland use, biodiversity, carbon stock, eco-tourism and local income
Amrit Dharohar focus: shift from high-volume tourism to high-value nature tourism
National Wetland Conservation Program (1986) is implemented through State Wetland Authorities
Wetlands Rules, 2017 notified by MoEFCC under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
Wetlands Rules decentralise management and provide for State or UT Wetlands Authorities
Wetland City Accreditation: part of the Ramsar Convention, approved at COP 12 in 2015
Accreditation requires all 6 international criteria and is valid for 6 years
Wetland City aim: conservation and wise use of urban and peri-urban wetlands

quizzes.passage: A wetland is a place in which the land is covered by water. That water may be salt, fresh or somewhere in between. Wetlands take many forms, so the term covers a wide range of landscapes. Lakes and rivers are among the most familiar of them, and swamps and wet grasslands also count as wetlands. Along the coast, mangroves are one of the forms the booklet describes, and coral reefs and other coastal areas appear in the same list. Marshes and bogs are also listed among the forms of wetlands. Some forms sit inland, while others lie near the sea. Wet grasslands and peatlands show that the water need not always form a lake. The booklet's list of water bodies is long, and it reaches from freshwater lakes to sea-edge habitats. The common feature in the definition is that land is covered by water, rather than any single shape or size. This is why a wetland can be a large lake, a river, a swamp or a stretch of grassland. The definition therefore allows a broad range of habitats to be counted within one category. Each of these forms is still a place where the land is covered by water. The booklet presents these forms as examples of a single category, which is the wetland.

quizzes.passage: The Ramsar Convention is an intergovernmental treaty that concerns wetlands. It is a formal agreement among its member countries, and it has 172 member states. The treaty focuses on wetlands of international importance. India is one of the countries that take part in the treaty. World Wetlands Day is observed every year to draw attention to wetlands and their value. Each year's observance carries a theme. The treaty takes its name from the Iranian city of Ramsar, where it was signed. The Montreux Record is a register of wetland sites. It records sites where changes in ecological character have occurred or are likely to occur. Such changes may result from technological developments, pollution or other human interference. Indian wetlands have appeared in the record. The Montreux Record is one of the tools linked to the treaty's work. Wetlands are areas of land covered by water, which may be salt, fresh or in between. The booklet describes wetlands as places with many water bodies, such as lakes, rivers and swamps. Wetlands are associated in the booklet with biodiversity and carbon stock. The booklet also notes that the treaty and World Wetlands Day share a focus on wetlands. Wetland conservation is therefore a shared concern for the countries in the treaty.
